1#_: (Siman 101 seif 1 in the hagahah) Only d'rabbanan it is not nullified. That is, where it is forbidden by law — such as an egg of nevelah, or poultry meat in milk, and the like; unlike meat that disappeared from sight, which is only a mere stringency — if it was mixed in the majority it is permitted on account of a double doubt — so too the Shach in his general rules (rules 17, 18, 19).
2#_: (Seif 2) And kosher in milk. And if it became forbidden through salting — from the words of Menachem Tzioni (21 s.k. 10) it appears there is no status of a piece worthy of honor; and in my humble opinion his proof can be rejected, also from the words of the Taz s.k. 4, for it is clear that in basar b'chalav d'rabbanan there is also the status of a piece worthy of honor.
3#_: (Taz s.k. 4) For there is a basar b'chalav prohibition here. I find this difficult: for above (seif 87) it is explained that curdling in the skin of a kosher stomach — if there is sixty in the milk it is permitted; thus through curdling it does not become basar b'chalav; and if curdled in the skin of neveilah it is forbidden only on account of neveilah, and it is no longer a prohibition on account of itself. Also according to what the Taz wrote (end of siman 87) that in impure meat with milk one cannot say each is permitted on its own — therefore it is not a prohibition on account of itself, and why should it also not be a piece worthy of honor? See there; if so, curdling in neveilah skin is more lenient, for it has no basar b'chalav status to judge it as a prohibition on account of itself, for one of them has a d'oraisa prohibition without the mixture — requires study. And on one difficulty one could say we are concerned perhaps there was sixty in the milk; but the second difficulty requires study.
4#_: (Seif 7) If one piece was cut. If a d'rabbanan prohibition was mixed — piece in pieces — one could say according to the Mechaber above (siman 99 seif 6) that it is permitted to cut them l'chatchila so they will be nullified, since they are already mixed; only that it is not nullified on account of being worthy of honor — we are not stringent regarding mixtures of one against one; and cutting them to nullify is like adding and nullifying — investigate.
5#_: (There) Permitted in any case. And why? One could say that if one of the pieces fell into a pot that has less than sixty portions of food and melted, it is permitted, since once melted its significance is lost and it is as if it was cut; and likewise if they removed it from the pot, nevertheless the pot is permitted, although the piece is forbidden — nevertheless one could say the gravy is permitted; see in Peri Megadim (siman 110 in the rules of double doubt, letter 10).
6#_: (Seif 8) A chicken with others. Perhaps specifically with others, for from the Torah it is nullified in this case we rely on resemblance; but not one against one. However, from the proof of the Gemara from the case of a piece of fish above (siman 83 seif 4) it implies that even d'oraisa we rely thus.
7#_: (Taz s.k. 15) And in my humble opinion there is nothing in this matter. And in the book Teshuvot Mateh Yosef (vol. 2 Yoreh Deah 6) he wrote that Rav Mohar Avraham, may his memory be blessed, in Salonika, and other rabbis, acted to permit.
